siaton2006PrimaryReport.citation: Carumbana, E. E. (2006). The limnology and fishery resources of the Siaton River in Southern Negros Oriental, Philippines. Unpublished report submitted to PREXIL, Negros Oriental State University.
siaton2006PrimaryReport.finding: The citation is verified in the publisher-hosted 2010 Negros–Siquijor checklist. A 2011 Silliman Journal article separately attributes 33 fish species in 28 families to this unpublished Siaton report.
siaton2006PrimaryReport.access: The primary report itself, a direct NORSU catalog entry, its fish list, and supporting methods/station tables were not located in this search.
siaton2006PrimaryReport.decision: Treat 33/28 only as a secondary-reported aggregate and discovery lead. It is not an independently checked count or an exportable checklist.

publisherChecklistAccessCorrection.source: Bucol and Carumbana (2010), Checklist of Fishes Found in the Fresh and Brackish Waters of Negros and Siquijor, Philippines.
publisherChecklistAccessCorrection.finding: An official Asian Journal of Biodiversity article page and publisher-hosted PDF were located and accessed; the earlier review had noted only the author-uploaded ResearchGate copy.
publisherChecklistAccessCorrection.access: Official publisher PDF confirms a tentative, multi-year compilation and describes Siaton collections from May 2004 to October 2005 at four stations. It says the samples were donated to the Smithsonian's USNM collection and includes selected Siaton locality/specimen notes.
publisherChecklistAccessCorrection.rights: Public access to the publisher PDF does not establish a reuse license. The broad 89-species compilation is not a current, complete or Siaton-only fish list.

laterReportOfSiatonCount.source: Bucol and Catid (2011 issue; publisher landing page displays 2022 platform date), Fishes and Macroinvertebrates of Señora River, Siquijor Island, Philippines.
laterReportOfSiatonCount.finding: The full article's discussion says the Siaton River report by Carumbana (2006, unpublished manuscript) reported 33 species in 28 families.
laterReportOfSiatonCount.limitations: This is a cross-reference within a separate Señora River study. It supplies no Siaton species-by-species table, collection dates, stations, voucher mapping or proof that the reported aggregate is the same as the 2004–2005 collection summarized in the 2010 checklist.

balananCommunityFisheryContext.source: Oracion and Hiponia, Nature and People Matter: Conservation and Ecotourism in Balanan Lake, Negros Oriental, Philippine Studies 57(1) (2009).
balananCommunityFisheryContext.finding: The article describes nonprobability interviews with 43 households in six sitios and reports that about one-third of respondent households fished in the lake; catch categories are common labels such as tilapia, eel, catfish, mudfish, shrimps and shells.
balananCommunityFisheryContext.limitations: This is historical social/livelihood context, not a fish sampling design. It does not provide scientific identifications, station-level records, catch dates by taxon, gear/effort, vouchers or a lake inventory.

decision.use: Use the 2006 Siaton report and the named Smithsonian voucher lots as acquisition leads. Use the Balanan paper only as dated livelihood context.
decision.reason: The underlying Siaton report is still unavailable. The accessible checklist is a tentative compilation and selected historical voucher lead, while Balanan's available fishery source uses common catch categories rather than taxonomic sampling.

limitations: The 33-species/28-family Siaton figure is a secondary citation until the 2006 report is obtained and checked.
The 2010 checklist's four-station Siaton collections and any selected museum lot identifiers must be reconciled to the original report before species-level inclusion.
A specimen collection date is historical evidence, not proof of current presence, abundance, catchability, legality, diet or safety.
The Balanan household study's common catch labels are not scientifically resolved taxa and cannot be converted to occurrence records.
No fish names, occurrence rows, abundance, geometry, diet records, safety alerts, map layers or public app rows were added.
No reuse license or publication approval was established for any checklist, interview text, table or structured derivative.
nextActions: Ask NORSU PREXIL and the report author for Carumbana's 2006 Siaton report, appendices, station names, survey dates, gear/effort, taxon list, voucher mapping and reuse terms.

Cross-check the 2010 publisher checklist's explicitly named USNM lots against Smithsonian/GBIF catalogue records before creating any occurrence rows; retain verbatim source names and dated locality scope.
Seek a primary Lake Balanan fish survey or BFAR/DENR fisheries dataset. Keep historical household catch categories separate from species occurrences and current catchability.
If the primary 2006 report remains unavailable, continue with individually verifiable museum vouchers and record the resulting evidence limits rather than claiming a complete Siaton list.

references.supports: Publisher-hosted 2010 checklist, its explicit tentative scope, 2004–2005 four-station Siaton collection and selected USNM specimen notes.
2011 Silliman Journal paper's secondary reference to Carumbana's 2006 Siaton report and the reported 33 species in 28 families.
Ateneo Archium bibliographic record for Oracion and Hiponia's Balanan community/ecotourism paper.
Accessible article text documenting the 43-household sample, livelihood context and common fishery catch labels.
